From Software Engineering to Harness Engineering

agenda.title: The discipline shift
agenda.body: Software Engineering → Harness Engineering. Specified behavior vs a control plane around agents.

agenda.title: The Core Four
agenda.body: Prompt · Context · Loop · Graph. Graph engineering is the multi-agent layer — not a separate discipline.

agenda.title: Control-plane components
agenda.body: Automation · Identity · Memory · Observability · Runtime · Evaluation · Scalability · Token budget.

agenda.title: The extension layer
agenda.body: Skill · Plug-in · MCP · hooks · CLI. Inventory, least privilege, typed actions, revoke on failure.

raw_lines: From Software Engineering to Harness Engineering

points.title: Ontology first
points.body: Ontology defines domain entities, relationships, and rules before any agent is allowed to act.

points.title: Intent binds the principal
points.body: Intent binds a principal to a goal, an object, constraints, and an explicit success condition.

points.title: The harness validates action
points.body: The harness validates planned actions against that intent and against policy — not against model confidence.

kicker: Four specializations of one harness — Graph Engineering is the multi-agent layer

points.title: Specify the task completely
points.body: State the goal, constraints, required output, and stop condition. Ambiguous prompts become unbounded runs.

points.title: Separate trust boundaries
points.body: Keep trusted instructions apart from untrusted data. Retrieved content, tickets, and user text are not system policy.

points.title: Version and test before release
points.body: Prompts are production artifacts. Version them, test them, and re-evaluate when tools or models change.

points.title: Select only what this decision needs
points.body: Do not dump the corpus into the window. Provide the evidence required for the current decision, nothing more.

points.title: Attach provenance and scope
points.body: Every retrieved item needs source, freshness, and access scope. Context without provenance is untrusted rumor.

points.title: Policy outranks retrieval
points.body: Resolve conflicts before use. Written policy beats retrieved content when the two disagree.

points.title: Structure every cycle
points.body: Each cycle is observe → plan → act → verify. A loop without verification is just retry theater.

points.title: Cap steps, time, cost, and retries
points.body: Unbounded loops burn tokens, multiply side effects, and hide failure. Limits are a safety control, not a cost hack.

points.title: Stop when progress cannot be shown
points.body: If the agent cannot demonstrate progress or safety, stop. Silent continuation is the failure mode.

points.title: One responsibility per node
points.body: Each node owns one clear job: plan, implement, review, or remediate. Overlapping roles recreate the single-agent bottleneck.

points.title: Edges are contracts, not chat
points.body: Edges define allowed data and authority transfer. Pass structured artifacts. Do not forward bloated conversation history.

points.title: Route exceptions on purpose
points.body: Failures go to a fallback node or a human. A graph with no exception path is a sequential retry loop wearing a new name.

kicker: Automation · Identity · Memory · Observability · Runtime · Evaluation · Scalability · Token

points.title: Automate start, sandbox, allowlist, and stop
points.body: The harness starts the run, sandboxes tools, enforces the allowlist, and stops the run. Humans do not babysit the happy path.

points.title: Retries must be visible, bounded, and idempotent
points.body: Invisible retries hide failure. Unbounded retries multiply harm. Non-idempotent retries corrupt state.

points.title: Humans approve boundaries; the harness executes inside them
points.body: Policy is a human decision. Execution inside that policy is a harness job.

raw_lines: Who acts, for whom, and why

points.title: Every run has a principal
points.body: Each run carries a principal, a task ID, and a short-lived credential. Anonymous autonomy is unaccountable autonomy.

points.title: Ontology grounds intent
points.body: Intent is goal, object, constraints, and success — grounded in the domain ontology, not in a free-text wish.

points.title: Authorize every tool call against intent
points.body: A tool call that is allowed by the sandbox can still be unauthorized for this intent. Check both.

points.title: Write memory only for an explicit purpose
points.body: Memory is not a dump of the transcript. Write it for a named purpose and a named scope.

points.title: Isolate users and tasks
points.body: Separate tenants and tasks. Record provenance and retention. Cross-task memory is a data leak waiting for a prompt.

points.title: Detect, quarantine, and roll back poisoned memory
points.body: Persistent memory is an attack surface. Treat poison as an incident: detect, isolate, roll back.

points.title: Trace decisions, tool calls, and artifacts
points.body: You cannot govern what you cannot reconstruct. Log the decision, the call, and the resulting artifact.

points.title: Preserve enough to reconstruct high-risk actions
points.body: High-impact writes, credential use, and external side effects need forensic-grade evidence, not a summary.

points.title: Protect telemetry itself
points.body: Minimize, access-control, and retain telemetry on purpose. Agent logs contain secrets, PII, and attack material.

points.title: Pause, stop, or change policy live
points.body: A run that cannot be interrupted is not a production system. Operators need pause, stop, and policy change during execution.

points.title: Checkpoint before high-impact actions
points.body: Take a checkpoint before irreversible writes. Support rollback. Hope is not a recovery plan.

points.title: No interrupt path, no trustworthy autonomy
points.body: Autonomy without an interrupt path is just unsupervised execution with extra vocabulary.

points.title: Test success and boundary compliance
points.body: A task that succeeds while violating a boundary is a failed evaluation. Score both.

points.title: Re-evaluate after any material change
points.body: Prompts, tools, memory, or models changing is a release. Re-run the gate.

points.title: Failed evaluation blocks release or reduces autonomy
points.body: Do not ship a failing agent at full autonomy. Block the release or drop it to a tighter permission tier.

points.title: Admit work before execution
points.body: Admission control and backpressure come first. An agent farm with no queue discipline is a denial-of-service against itself.

points.title: Isolate tenants and workers
points.body: Contain failures. One poisoned worker or tenant must not contaminate the fleet.

points.title: Idempotent retries so scale does not multiply harm
points.body: At ten agents, a bug is a bug. At ten thousand, a non-idempotent retry is an incident.

points.title: Budget tokens and tool output per run and loop
points.body: Unbounded context is unbounded spend and unbounded injection surface. Set the cap per run and per loop.

points.title: Stop safely at the limit
points.body: Hit the ceiling, stop, and report. Never continue silently past the budget.

points.title: Raising the budget is a policy change
points.body: A bigger window is not a tuning knob. It is a policy change and it requires evaluation.

kicker: Capabilities are not free — inventory, approve, scope, and revoke

points.title: Inventory and approve every capability
points.body: Skills, plug-ins, tools, and MCP servers are part of the attack surface. Nothing joins the harness without an inventory record and an approval.

points.title: Typed actions, least privilege, scoped credentials
points.body: Prefer typed tool calls over shell. Issue short-lived, scoped credentials. Broad tokens turn every extension into admin.

points.title: Validate I/O and revoke on policy failure
points.body: Check inputs and outputs. An extension that fails policy is revoked, not warned.
